title: IT Helpdesk Remote Update Request — Ops Workstation

transcript.speaker: IT Helpdesk
transcript.text: Hi, this is the IT helpdesk. We're seeing some unusual activity on your workstation — it looks like your antivirus may be out of date. I need to push a remote update. Can you go to Settings, then Remote Desktop, and enable remote connections? It'll only take a minute. I'll do everything from my end.

transcript.speaker: Ops Workstation 1
transcript.text: Wait — I don't recall reporting that. What's your name and extension?

transcript.speaker: IT Helpdesk
transcript.text: I'm with IT — I'm handling a batch of remote updates today. Just need you to enable Remote Desktop for five seconds. I’ll confirm the patch was applied right after.

transcript.speaker: Ops Workstation 1
transcript.text: I’ll call the helpdesk directly to verify. Hold on.

voiceStyles.IT Helpdesk: Male, calm, professional, slight technical jargon

instructorNote: This is a fake IT helpdesk call using the 'helpfulness' and 'technical jargon' social engineering pattern. The correct response is to not comply and to verify the call via official contact. Watch for immediate compliance or hesitation due to pressure.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Terminal Incident Response Plan (TIRP)
citations.headingPath: TIRP › Section 13 › 13.4 Scenario A: Ransomware / Critical Network Failure
citations.quote: **Impact:** airport computers locked; files encrypted; airline systems (separate networks) may be unaffected, but airport-provided systems (FIDS, BHS) fail. **Response:** IT — isolate the network; ord
